    1-2

    Lecture 1-2

    How do the simulator's numbers become evidence you can argue with?

    Lecture 1-2 · the plan

    From trends to an evidence register

    1. Three pulls from the tabrun, snapshot and event log, each tagged with a role
    2. The route without the tabCSV export from the OTS, then drop it in the workbook
    3. Reading the TE-1 trendswhich tags moved, when, and which did not
    4. Fact, inference or opinionsorting what you measured from what you were told

    From this OTS (live)

    Three pulls, three kinds of evidence

    The workbook is set up. Its first job is to bring the simulator in as evidence.

    Run

    Every distributed control system (DCS) trend, in time.

    Snapshot

    Every reading now, beside its design value.

    Event log

    Alarms, trips, actions, phone and lab answers.

    Each pull is a comma-separated values (CSV) dataset with a role: Initial run, Plant test or Fix.

    In the tab

    One button, three datasets

    • Pick the role first, then Pull all three.
    • Pull again after each plant test and after the fix.
    • In the student edition the log hides the instructor's fault lines.

    Standalone copies

    Export from the OTS, drop into the workbook

    Interactive — real TE-1 run

    What moved, and what did not?

    Each line is the change from design. The products move; TIC-401, PIC-420 and TCV-401 stay flat.

    Evidence register

    The workbook drafts the evidence lines

    • Suggest evidence turns a dataset into lines: deviations, on-design readings, alarms, changes.
    • On-design readings feed IS / IS NOT: where the problem could be but is not.
    • You keep, edit or delete each line.

    Interactive — sort each statement

    Fact, inference or opinion?

    A computed number is an inference: it is only as good as the instruments behind it.

    1-3

    Lecture 1-3

    TE-1, part 1: what exactly is wrong, and what could cause it?

    Lecture 1-3 · the plan

    Engage, Define, Explore on a real run

    1. The case as the board sees itExample 1.1: TE-1 after 20 minutes, no action taken
    2. Engageis it time-critical, and what do we tell people
    3. Definea problem statement that names no cause, and IS / IS NOT
    4. Explorea butane balance on the outlets tells what came in
    5. Hypotheses screenedS / D / N against the evidence

    Example 1.1 · problem statement · read first

    EXAMPLE 1.1TE-1 · Bottoms off spec since the tank switch

    Situation given

    “Unit lined out. After lunch AI-410 creeps toward the 28 wt% spec and FI-420 is higher than this morning. TIC-401 and PIC-420 are at their set points.” You load TE-1 and let it run 20 minutes without touching anything.

    (a) Decide whether it is time-critical. (b) Write the problem statement and the IS / IS NOT table. (c) Check what came in with a balance, then list and screen hypotheses.

    TagDesign00:20
    AI-410 bottoms C4, wt% (≤ 28)26.5627.93
    AI-420 vapour C4, wt% (≥ 75)76.8279.16
    FI-420 vapour, Nm³/h611662
    FIC-410 liquid, m³/h14.0313.71
    TI-410 flash, °C49.2348.01
    TIC-401 hot feed, °C74.074.0
    PIC-420 drum, kPa g102.7102.7
    TCV-401 to E-400, %30.530.4
    FIC-400 feed, m³/h16.0016.00
    Alarms 00:00–00:20—none

    AI = analyser, FI = flow indicator, TI = temperature indicator, TIC / PIC = temperature / pressure controller. Values from the TE-1 run.

    Stage 1 · Engage

    EXAMPLE 1.1Time-critical? Not yetstep 1 of 6

    ConsequenceAt risk?Why
    SafetyNo102.7 kPa g against a 250 kPa g trip; level 50 %
    EnvironmentNoPSV-400 quiet, flare at pilot
    EquipmentNonothing near a limit
    ProductionYesAI-410 rising 0.07 wt%/min toward 28
    Decision: keep running and investigate with cheap checks; be ready to move TIC-401 / PIC-420.

    Stage 2 · Define

    EXAMPLE 1.1A statement that names no causestep 2 of 6

    The butane in the D-400 bottoms (AI-410) rose from 26.56 to 27.93 wt% with FI-420 up 8 % and TI-410 down 1.2 °C, against a 28 wt% spec, by 00:20:00, with TIC-401 and PIC-420 at their set points.

    “The feed got lighter” would be a cause; it stays out.

    Stage 2 · Define

    EXAMPLE 1.1IS / IS NOT kills whole familiesstep 3 of 6

    The heat input is not short: TCV-401, TI-402, TI-403 and FI-405 sit on design.

    Stage 3 · Explore

    EXAMPLE 1.1A butane balance on the outletsstep 4 of 6

    D-400 has no feed analyser. The two outlets can still tell what came in.

    $F,\,V,\,L$
    feed, vapour and liquid mass flows
    kg/h
    $z$
    butane mass fraction in the feed (not measured)
    wt%
    $y$
    butane in the vapour, read on AI-420
    wt%
    $x$
    butane in the liquid, read on AI-410
    wt%
    $$F\,z=V\,y+L\,x\qquad F=V+L$$

    Stage 3 · Explore

    EXAMPLE 1.1First, check it closes at designstep 5 of 6

    From the previous slide$F\,z=V\,y+L\,x$
    $V\,y+L\,x=1714\times0.7682+8427\times0.2656=3555\ \text{kg/h}$outlets at design, from the run data
    $z=\dfrac{3555}{10141}=35.1\ \text{wt\%}$design feed is 35 wt%: the meters agree

    Assumes steady state and that FI-420, FIC-410 and both analysers read right.

    Stage 3 · Explore

    EXAMPLE 1.1At 00:20 more butane leaves than came instep 6 of 6

    Butane balance$F\,z=V\,y+L\,x$
    $V\,y+L\,x=1842\times0.7916+8299\times0.2793=3776\ \text{kg/h}$outlets at 00:20 (3780 in the workbook)
    $z=\dfrac{3776}{10141}=37.2\ \text{wt\%}$a 35 wt% feed would bring only 3549 kg/h

    The outlets say the feed holds about 37 wt% butane: more came in, or one meter is wrong. The lab decides.

    Interactive — move the readings

    What feed do the outlets imply?

    Stage 3 balance$z=(V\,y+L\,x)/F$
    Butane out
    Implied feed $z$
    Design feed35.0 wt%

    $F$ = 10 141 kg/h, $L=F-V$. Every reading that moved points the same way: more butane came in.

    Stage 3 · Explore

    EXAMPLE 1.1Seven hypotheses on six branches

    Each idea becomes a working hypothesis (WH-n) with an “if … then we should observe” and a falsifier.

    Interactive — click a cell: S, D, N

    Screen the hypotheses against the evidence

    S supports, D denies, N neutral. One D is enough to kill a cause; the DCS alone already leaves few standing.

    Lecture 1-3 · summary

    What section 1-3 settled

    • TE-1 costs product quality, not safety: keep running and investigate.
    • The statement names the symptom with numbers, never a cause.
    • At fixed T and P the products tell what came in.
    • S / D / N leaves the causes that only tests can separate.

    Lecture 1-4

    TE-1, part 2: which test settles it, what fix, and what do we keep?

    Lecture 1-4 · the plan

    Plan, Do it, Look back, hand in

    1. Cheap tests firsttrend review, field walk, telephone, laboratory
    2. Predict the move on a copychoose the set points before touching the plant
    3. Do itresults, the fix, and actual against predicted
    4. The ledger, Look back and hand incost and value, a rule, a barrier, the report and the .woods.json

    Example 1.2 · problem statement · read first

    EXAMPLE 1.2TE-1 continued · test, then fix

    Example 1.1: at 00:20 AI-410 27.93 wt% (spec 28), FI-420 662 Nm³/h (611), TI-410 48.01 °C (49.23); TIC-401, PIC-420, TCV-401 on design; outlets imply a 37 wt% feed.

    Seven working hypotheses (WH) on six branches; the DCS already denies most of them.

    (a) Plan cheap Look tests with predictions. (b) Run them and judge each WH. (c) Predict the fix on an offline copy and make it once. (d) Close the cost ledger.

    TestClassCost
    T-1 trend reviewA · read data0
    T-2 field walkB · look0
    T-3 telephoneB · look0
    T-4 laboratoryC · buyUSD 150
    T-5 set pointsD · change0

    Stage 4 · Plan

    EXAMPLE 1.2Predict before you lookstep 1 of 5

    A test is worth running only where the survivors' predictions differ.

    TestIf WH-1 feed lighterIf WH-3 PT-420 lowIf WH-4 AI-410 drift
    T-2 fieldPG-420 = PIC-420PG-420 above PIC-420PG-420 = PIC-420
    T-3 phonea tank change reportednothing reportednothing reported
    T-4 labfeed > 35, bottoms = AI-410bottoms = AI-410bottoms below AI-410

    Look and buy tests disturb nothing, so they come before any move of TIC-401 or PIC-420.

    Stage 5 · Do it

    EXAMPLE 1.2The workbook records each verdictstep 2 of 5

    • T-2: PG-420 103 kPa g, stems where the outputs say: WH-2, 3, 5 killed.
    • T-3: “the feed tank was switched this morning”: WH-6 killed.
    • T-4: feed 38.0, bottoms 28.2 wt% (AI-410 28.15): WH-4 killed.

    Interactive — pick a move

    Predict the fix on a copystep 3 of 5

    AI-410 after 40 min
    Spec / alarm clears below28.00 / 27.72 wt%

    The OTS runs an offline copy for 40 minutes. 78 °C / 98 kPa g clears the alarm with 1 °C left below TIC-401 HI.

    Stage 5 · Do it

    EXAMPLE 1.2Move once, then comparestep 4 of 5

    • 00:24:40: TIC-401 74 → 78 °C, PIC-420 102.7 → 98 kPa g.
    • AI-410 peaks at 28.16, is below 28 at 00:29:40; the alarm clears at 00:46:33.
    • 01:04:40: AI-410 27.63, AI-420 78.01 wt%: all four predictions met.

    Stage 4 → 6 · the ledger

    EXAMPLE 1.2What it cost, what it is worthstep 5 of 5

    $$V=(m_{fix}-m_{off})\times h$$
    $m_{fix}$
    margin after the fix, from the profitability display
    429 $/h
    $m_{off}$
    margin if left alone, offline copy at 74 °C / 102.7 kPa g
    −158 $/h
    $h$
    hours until the tank is changed (assumed one shift)
    8 h

    $V$ ≈ USD 4 700 recovered against USD 228 spent (lab 150, lost margin 78).

    Interactive — change the assumptions

    Was the diagnosis worth it?

    From the previous slide$V=(m_{fix}-m_{off})\times h$
    Value recovered
    Spent
    Net

    Off spec, the unit loses money every hour; the cheap tests pay back within minutes.

    Stage 6 · Look back

    Keep the rule, add a barrier

    The product is back. What stops the next tank switch from costing a shift?

    Training rule: when both products move and the controllers have not, look at the feed before the instruments: ask what changed upstream and sample it.
    • Procedure: sample every new feed tank before line-up; the tank farm calls the board before every switch.
    • Barrier (proposed): a feed analyser with feed-forward to the TIC-401 / PIC-420 set points.
    • New problem: when the feed returns to 35 wt%, the set points must come back, or the vapour goes heavy.

    Outputs

    Save, report, present

    • Save writes the project as .woods.json; Open brings it back on any copy.
    • Word report and team slides are built from what you filled.
    • Hand in the .woods.json, the report and the Debrief score.

    Class Activity

    Can you solve it yourself?

    Class activity · the plan

    Two cases, situation text only

    TE-1 was solved for you. Now the same method on cases whose answers you do not have.

    1. Problem 1.1 · TE-3Stage 0 to the problem statement: pulls, urgency, IS / IS NOT (practises 1-2 and 1-3)
    2. Problem 1.2 · TE-7hypotheses, S / D / N and a test plan with predictions (practises 1-3 and 1-4)

    Problem 1.1 · statement · read first

    PROBLEM 1.1TE-3 · Drum pressure creeping up

    Situation given

    “Unit lined out. PIC-420 has drifted above its set point and its output is 100 %.”

    Load TE-3 on Exercises and let it run 20 minutes without acting. In the workbook:

    (a) pull the run, the snapshot and the event log with role Initial run; (b) fill 0.2 and 0.4 with numbers and times; (c) decide in 1.3–1.4 whether it is time-critical; (d) write the IS / IS NOT table and the problem statement 2.11, naming no cause.

    Problem 1.1 · how to set it up

    PROBLEM 1.1Run it, pull it, define it

    StepWhereReport
    Load TE-3, run 20 minExercisestime of each change
    Pull all threelive cardrole Initial run
    Suggest evidenceeach datasetdeviations, on-design
    Engage, DefineStages 1–2urgency, IS / IS NOT, 2.11

    Done when 2.11 is one sentence with numbers and no cause. Watch the distance to PSHH-426.

    Problem 1.2 · statement · read first

    PROBLEM 1.2TE-7 · TIC-401 below set point, TCV-401 at 100 %

    Situation given

    “Unit lined out. Over the shift TIC-401 has fallen to about 67 °C with TCV-401 wide open.”

    Load TE-7 and run it until TCV-401 reaches 100 %. In the workbook:

    (a) pull the data; (b) build the fishbone with at least one idea per branch and five hypotheses with “if … then” and a falsifier; (c) screen them with S / D / N; (d) plan Look tests and one Change test with predictions, stop and back-out rules; (e) run them and judge each hypothesis.

    Problem 1.2 · how to set it up

    PROBLEM 1.2Hypotheses first, tests second

    StepWhereReport
    Trends from loadTrend explorerwhich tag moved first, and when
    Fishbone, WH list3.4 and 3.6≥ 5 hypotheses, six branches
    S / D / N4.3survivors and why
    Tests4.6, then 5.0predictions, results, verdicts

    A test is useful only if two survivors predict different results. A heat balance on E-400 is a good start.

    Before you go

    Key Takeaways

    1

    Pull run, snapshot and log with a role, after every move.

    2

    State the symptom with numbers; name no cause in 2.11.

    3

    Products moved, settings did not: check what came in.

    4

    Choose tests whose predictions differ; predict the fix on a copy.

    5

    Close the ledger and keep one rule and one barrier.
